newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest stock prices up in strong demand.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest stock prices up in strong demand.

text.p: The Bucharest bourse closed Thursday with the bulk of its stocks gaining in both average and closing prices as demand outstripped supply.
"Buying interest, mostly from foreigners, was strong and we're in for further leaps tommorow as plenty of buy notes were left in the market," said a trader.

Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, rose by 1.2, 1.43 and 1.24 percent respectively from Wednesday, climbing to new highs for the year.
Twenty-two stocks posted gains in their average prices, eight lost and five stayed flat. Eight stocks had no deal and two were suspended, a bourse report showed.
Volume grew slightly to three million shares from 2.9 million and turnover shed some 300 million lei to 12.5 billion.
Operators said the session's key players had been foreign investors, taking heart from improved investment legislation -- including portfolio rules -- and unimpressed by a firmer leu.

"Foreigners changed their hard currency days ago, so there was no reverberation in the market," a broker said. "But if the leu gains further ground and stock prices continue to rise then we might see an effect as shares would grow expensive."
Buying was most active on the first tier, with pressure building up in late trading to pull five of the seven high-caps to a higher close. The section had 9.6 billion lei in turnover.

Antibiotice and Terapia added 250 and 200 lei respectively to 7,550 and 7,700. Chemical plant Oltchim ended 50 lei higher at 3,600, Compa vehicle parts maker firmed 300 lei to 3,200 and fertiliser maker Azomures gained 150 lei to 3,950.
The section's sole loser was Sofert fertiliser maker, which weakened 500 lei to 32,500. Traders said Sofert market price was viewed as high. Arctic refrigerator maker remained suspended.

The second tier's most active stock was Policolor dye maker. It took almost half the section's turnover level of 2.9 billion lei and closed 150 lei higher at 6,550. Its shares will start being traded on the first tier on Friday.
